newsitem.title: USA: Chubais sees better Russia credit rating.
newsitem.headline: Chubais sees better Russia credit rating.

text.p: Membership of the Paris Club of creditor states should help Russia win a better credit rating, once the ratings are reassessed this fall, reform chief Anatoly Chubais said on Saturday.

Chubais, one of two first deputy prime ministers in the Russian government also said he expected a final agreement on the restructuring of Russia's commercial bank debts by the summer. "All the main problems with the London Club have been overcome," he said.
Russia, which inherited responsibility for both the debts and the liabilities of the former Soviet Union, owes comercial banks some $33 billion, according to Russian figures.
The Russian Central Bank said this week that it expected a deal with the London Club of commercial bank creditors would be closed by August 15.
Chubais said Russian membership of the Paris Club as a creditor would help Russia win a better rating for its own debt.
"We would be given a higher rating now than we were at the end of last year," he said. "We will apply again next fall and I believe Russia's rating will rise."

Russia has a Ba2 rating from Moody's, BB- from S&P and BB+ from IBCA. It raised $2 billion this week with a 10-year Eurobond, its third issue as a sovereign borrower and the largest single issue from an emerging market economy.
